newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares continue lower on heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares continue lower on heavy selling.

text.p: Nigerian share prices ended weaker on Wednesday, weighed down by heavy selling, dealers said.
The all-share index fell to 8374.66 from 8405.60 on Tuesday.
Traders said selling of blue chips persisted because cash-starved investors were offloading to re-invest in cheaper stocks.
Food shares were hardest hit but troubled oil marketing and conglomerate shares also saw big falls, they said.
Nestle, whose disappointing first quarter result recently sparked worry that Nigerian companies were yet to recover from economic depression, fell 10 kobo to 51.70 naira.
Flour Mills was 16.00 naira, down 65 kobo on fears that it too would post declining profits, traders said.
Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company closed 30 kobo lower at 51.65 naira.
Lack of interest in the oil marketers cost African Petroleum and Unipetrol a 50 kobo loss each to 53.50 naira and 66.00 naira, respectively.
Agip at 15.25 naira and National Oil at 50.75 naira were each down 15 kobo.
Nigerian Breweries ended 17.80 naira, 20 kobo lower in its consistent slide.
Conglomerate UAC dropped 30 kobo to 15.10 naira while Lever Brothers was five kobo weaker at 26.30 naira.
Some banks ended stronger on a current positive perception but dealers said the number was fewer than in recent days.
United Bank for Africa (UBA) maintained its upswing, rising 15 kobo to 13.35 naira. Newly-listed Co-Operative Bank gained one kobo at 1.06 naira, the same as Owena Bank which ended at 1.42 naira.
Guinness closed at 8.05 naira, five kobo higher, the same margin as oil miller P.S. Mandrides at 7.05 naira.
